I believe that in this war of Russia against Ukraine, there are prospects for a peaceful settlement. Of course there are moments of frustration, internal issues, war related complications, all sorts of trouble. But nevertheless, we must understand one thing: Ukraine wants peace, President Trump wants peace – which means we are allies on this issue, and there should be no doubt about it. We must move toward this goal. Ukraine wants peace much more than Putin does. Yet Putin does everything to make it look as though he wants peace and Ukraine does not. These are signals he sends to America. This is not true; it is manipulation. I very much want the U.S. to trust us, because we are their partners. Even when help was needed in the Middle East, we responded immediately to the request. That is what being allies all about. We need to keep looking each day for ways to reach a peace agreement. We need to meet with the Americans. We have a couple more ideas on how we can force this war to end. From an interview with New York Post (5/5).

Russia mobilizes 40–45 thousand people every month. We must eliminate roughly the same number of troops so that the Russian army doesn’t grow in size. Eliminate them simply so that Russia cannot expand its aggression. Over the past three months, we eliminated 30, 35, and 28 thousand Russian soldiers respectively. That is almost 100 thousand people. Just imagine how much Russia is sacrificing for this war. From an interview with New York Post (4/5).

The discovery of californium was announced 76 years ago on this day, after it was synthesized by a team of physicists at the University of California Radiation Laboratory in Berkeley @UCBerkeley. Each microgram of fresh californium produces 139 million neutrons per minute, which makes it a strong neutron emitter. This makes californium useful for some nuclear reactors that rely on neutrons as a start-up source for chain reactions. These californium-emitted neutrons are also an effective tool in healthcare. They can be used to treat certain types of cervical and brain cancers, particularly when other radiation therapies are ineffective.

He stated that seafarers are the “unsung heroes of global trade,” who, despite challenging conditions and long periods away from their families, ensure the seamless movement of essential cargo across the world. Referring to the recent developments in the region, he highlighted how both vessels demonstrated exceptional resilience and composure while navigating high-risk conditions, ensuring the safe delivery of vital LPG cargo, contributing to India’s energy security. We are pleased to welcome Dr. Atindra Nath Mondal to the Trinamool Congress family. A distinguished medical professional and seasoned public health administrator, he currently serves as the Additional Medical Superintendent at the College of Medicine & JNM Hospital, Kalyani, in Nadia. Over the years, he has held several key administrative positions, including Medical Superintendent of Ranaghat Sub-Divisional Hospital and Deputy Medical Superintendent at SSKM Hospital, Kolkata. With a strong academic foundation, holding an MBBS and DPH from Calcutta University, along with an MBA in Hospital Administration, he brings with him extensive experience in managing healthcare institutions across both rural and urban settings. His career reflects a deep understanding of public health systems and a sustained commitment to improving healthcare delivery. We extend a warm welcome and look forward to his valuable contributions in further strengthening our collective efforts towards people-centric progress.

🌋 40 years of Mount Etna eruptions through the eyes of our satellites 📍 Mount Etna — Sicily, Italy In the 1980s, when Etna erupted, we watched from afar. Limited resolution and revisit times. Days before data could be fully analysed. The volcano was active, but our eyes in space were still learning to see. Today, the volcano still stands, but in a completely different technological era. Our Earth observation ecosystem is now much faster, sharper and smarter. Thanks to satellite imagery, we’ve been able to track four decades of eruptions, lava flows, and landscape transformations with unprecedented precision: 📈 Better understanding volcanic dynamics ⚡ Anticipating risks 🚒 Protecting communities and infrastructure 🔬 Supporting scientific research 👇📸 These SPOT satellite images of Mount Etna, captured between 1989 and 2025, are more than a geological timeline. What makes them truly fascinating is not only the volcanic activity itself, but also the technological revolution behind these images seen from space. As a bonus, the last snapshot below is an Amplitude Change Detection image. Created from 4 individual acquisitions performed by our Radar Constellation, its colorisation shows the structural changes of the volcano’s surface between 2008 and 2019. 📸 Want to explore the SPOT 6 image in full resolution? Kasaragod is the northern gateway of Keralam and an important railway corridor connecting the state with Karnataka and the rest of India. Unfortunately, despite heavy passenger movement, railway connectivity in this region remains extremely inadequate. The people of Kasaragod are not asking for luxury trains or prestigious announcements. Their demand is simple—basic train services, proper stoppages, and reliable connectivity. The state of the UK's armed forces, once the envy of empires, is now a fading shadow of its former self. It's so hollowed out that the British Army has only about 50,000 medically deployable soldiers out of a total of 73,000, making it the smallest since the Napoleonic Wars. It's also shrinking further, with net 300 soldiers leaving each month. With reserves, the UK could currently mobilize 180,000. Maybe you think this doesn't sound so bad. Let me put these numbers in context. My home country of Singapore (a former British colony) is a tiny island nation state with a population of 6 million. The UK's is more than 10X larger at 68 million. Yet, the Singapore Armed Forces has 51,000 full-time active personnel and it can mobilize a total force of >300,000 (with reserves). That's 300,00 for a population of 6 million (Singapore) compared to 180,000 for a population of 68 million (UK). Al Jazeera claims, based on estimated figures from the 12-day war, that Iran possessed up to 2,500 missiles at the start of that conflict. I don’t even know where to begin, because both ends of that claim are wrong, both the 2,500 estimate itself and the assumption that the post-12-day-war inventory has remained unchanged until today. Any analysis of another country’s military inventory must be based on production timelines, supply chains, and comparative industrial capacity. North Korea, whose missile industry is roughly one-third the size of Iran’s, is capable of commissioning up to 1,000 missiles in a single ceremony. Estimates suggest Russia produces around 2,500-3,000 missiles per year. And Iran? The Persians began producing missiles in the late 1980s and early 1990s. Since then, they have never stopped stockpiling. In the eight months since the end of the 12-day war, if Iran had done nothing but refurbishing old missiles, factoring in its domestic fuel production, it would already have added 700-1,000 missiles to its stockpile. But Iran has done far more than that. The most likely scenario is that, in this same period, it has added 2 to 4 times that number. Iran is a missile country. They don’t have a decent air force, or strong navy or armored vehicles. They are focused on missiles. Iran currently manufactures around 15–20 different models and variants of ballistic and cruise missiles, including anti-ship missiles. How many of each model does it produce annually? And it has been simultaneously producing more than 10 models for over a decade. How many missiles do you think it has accumulated? Certainly far more than 2,500. The reduction in Iranian launches is due to the destruction or burial of silos and launch ramps in successive coalition strikes, but also by deliberate choice, a strategy of prolonged war of attrition. In this phase, production will be deliberately kept low and resources carefully rationed. The exact same thing is happening with the US and Israel. Their main shortages are interceptors and precision-guided munitions, two categories that take a long time to manufacture. China was the first country to establish diplomatic relations with Turkmenistan. It was also among the earliest supporters of Turkmenistan's policy of permanent neutrality and the first to formalize a strategic partnership with the country through a political document. The friendship between the two nations dates back more than 2,000 years. Along the ancient Silk Road, Chinese silk and porcelain reached Central Asia, while Turkmenistan's famed Akhal-Teke horse, known in China as the "sweat blood horse," became a symbol of early exchanges between the two peoples. Modern diplomatic ties began on January 6, 1992, when the two countries signed a joint statement and established ambassadorial relations. Today, cooperation continues to deepen in culture, education, media and sports. Local partnerships are also growing, including the sister province relationship between northwest China's Shaanxi Province and Turkmenistan's Mary region. From the Silk Road to today, China and Turkmenistan continue to write new chapters of friendship built on mutual respect and shared development. IoT-Driven Water Management in Rural Tamil Nadu In Erode district, Tamil Nadu, an IoT-enabled smart water management system has been introduced to improve efficiency in rural water supply networks. Using sensors to monitor tank levels and automate pump operations, the system enables real-time management of overhead tanks and prevents overflow, ensuring more reliable water distribution. Deployed across 50 habitations in 16 villages, the solution has delivered a 40% reduction in electricity costs, 50% lower electricity consumption, and a 20% increase in water supply. In Ponmudi village alone, daily water availability increased by 44,180 litres. The initiative demonstrates how technology-led, institution-driven solutions can improve water efficiency, reduce operational costs, and strengthen sustainable rural infrastructure. I decided to kind of spice things up a bit and pivot to malware defense stuff. I explored different thingies and fell down the rabbit hole of YARA stuff. I didn't want to dive into something like minifilters. I've got this goofy setup where I can extract YARA rules from Windows Defender because of the research from @_t_tani. I've got like, 20,000 YARA rules, or something, I don't know. It's a lot. Regardless, I was like, "maybe I should make a shrimple file scanner with all these YARA rules". This is what a basic static analysis engine does in usermode. I saw a lot of people being like, "JUST YARA.EXE --FILE", and I was like, "that's kind of lame". I started bonking the YARA open source repo looking at different stuff. I then had to fight YARA open source stuff because libyara64.lib wants to fight you to become libyara64.dll. People on GitHub complained too, but whatever, I figured it out. My next goal is transform all the YARA rules into YARAC, or whatever it's called. In theory, I could then take a binary, or directory, and then use the YARA analysis engine to compare it to all the Microsoft YARA rules. I then considered implementing basic parameters, or maybe a goofy ass UI, or something. I then realized I'm basically making THORLite-Lite.

বেগম খালেদা জিয়ার নামাজে জানাজায় নারীদের জন্য বিশেষ ব্যবস্থা ঢাকা, ৩০ ডিসেম্বর ২০২৫: বাংলাদেশ জাতীয়তাবাদী দল (বিএনপি)-এর চেয়ারপার্সন, তিনবারের সাবেক প্রধানমন্ত্রী ও গণতান্ত্রিক রাজনীতির শীর্ষ নেত্রী বেগম খালেদা জিয়ার ইন্তেকালে দেশব্যাপী গভীর শোকের আবহ বিরাজ করছে। তাঁর প্রতি শেষ শ্রদ্ধা জানাতে সর্বস্তরের মানুষের অংশগ্রহণ নিশ্চিত করতে প্রয়োজনীয় প্রস্তুতি গ্রহণ করা হয়েছে অন্তর্বর্তীকালীন সরকার। এই প্রেক্ষাপটে বেগম খালেদা জিয়ার নামাজে জানাজায় অংশগ্রহণ করতে ইচ্ছুক নারীদের জন্য বিশেষ ব্যবস্থা রাখা হয়েছে। জাতীয় সংসদ ভবনের দক্ষিণ প্লাজা ও মানিক মিয়া এভিনিউ এলাকায় নারীদের জন্য পৃথকভাবে এ বিশেষ ব্যবস্থা করা হয়েছে, যাতে তাঁরা সুশৃঙ্খল ও নিরাপদ পরিবেশে জানাজায় অংশ নিতে পারেন। উল্লেখ্য, বেগম খালেদা জিয়ার নামাজে জানাজা বাদ জোহর বেলা দুইটায় অনুষ্ঠিত হবে। জানাজায় অংশগ্রহণে আগ্রহী সকলকে নিরাপত্তাজনিত কারণে কোনো প্রকার ব্যাগ বহন না করার জন্য অনুরোধ জানানো হচ্ছে। বেগম খালেদা জিয়াকে শেষ বিদায় জানাতে আগত সকলের সার্বিক নিরাপত্তা ও শৃঙ্খলা নিশ্চিত করতে সংশ্লিষ্ট কর্তৃপক্ষ প্রয়োজনীয় সব ধরনের ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করেছে।

दक्षिण भारतीय सांस्कृतिक विरासत का संवर्धन भारत सरकार संस्कृति मंत्रालय के अधीन स्वायत्त निकायों के माध्यम से दक्षिण भारतीय सांस्कृतिक विरासत को बढ़ावा देती है, जिनमें कलाक्षेत्र फाउंडेशन (चेन्नई), संगीत नाटक अकादमी और दक्षिण क्षेत्र सांस्कृतिक केंद्र (तंजावुर) शामिल हैं। ये संगठन क्षेत्र में सांस्कृतिक परंपराओं के संवर्धन और संरक्षण के लिए प्रशिक्षण, प्रदर्शन, अनुसंधान, प्रलेखन, कार्यशालाओं और उत्सवों जैसे विभिन्न कार्यक्रम और कार्यकलाप संचालित करते हैं। प्रमुख पहलों में भरतनाट्यम और कर्नाटक संगीत का प्रशिक्षण, लोक और जनजातीय कला रूपों को समर्थन और कूड़ियाट्टम, पुलिकली, छाया कठपुतली और थोलपावकूठू आदि पारंपरिक कलाओं का प्रलेखन और संवर्धन शामिल हैं। विस्तृत जानकारी: pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.…

Today in San José, Costa Rica, I had the honor of opening the Ninth Assembly of the OAS Inter-American Telecommunication Commission @OEA_CITEL. I thanked the Government of Costa Rica @micittcr for hosting this important gathering and recognized the continued commitment of @OAS_official Member States, regulators, industry, academia, and the technical community to advancing connectivity across the Americas. Communication and connectivity have long been central to the inter-American system. As early as the First International American Conference in 1890, our countries envisioned linking the Hemisphere through shared communications infrastructure. Today, through CITEL, the Organization of American States continues that tradition by strengthening regional cooperation on telecommunications and digital technologies. Telecommunications are no longer simply a sector of the economy; they are the backbone of modern society. Expanding meaningful connectivity, modernizing regulatory frameworks, and strengthening digital ecosystems are essential for innovation, education, healthcare, and democratic participation throughout our region. The San José Declaration reflects the shared commitment of our Member States to advance universal connectivity, resilient digital infrastructure, and stronger collaboration among governments, industry, academia, and civil society. Through dialogue and partnership, we can build a more connected, innovative, and inclusive Americas.

UNA INESPERADA CONEXIÓN ENTRE EL POLEN, LA INMUNIDAD Y LA EXTINCIÓN DE LOS MAMUTS SORPRENDE A LA CIENCIA El hallazgo de restos de mamuts con indicios de alergia al polen ha generado nuevas hipótesis sobre las causas de su desaparición. Un equipo de investigadores de Austria, Rusia e Israel, respaldados por instituciones académicas en sus respectivos países, detectó fragmentos de inmunoglobulina en fósiles, lo que sugiere que estos animales pudieron haber desarrollado enfermedades alérgicas graves cuando la concentración de polen aumentó durante el deshielo global. Según un artículo publicado en la revista científica Earth History and Biodiversity —especializada en paleobiología y estudios evolutivos— y difundido por Muy Interesante, la presencia anómala de inmunoglobulinas, proteínas asociadas a respuestas alérgicas, coincidía con periodos de mayor abundancia de polen en los registros paleoclimáticos. Los restos analizados proceden de yacimientos en Siberia, donde las condiciones de conservación permitieron el estudio detallado de moléculas biológicas que normalmente no sobreviven al paso del tiempo. 📲 Leé la nota completa 🔗 infob.ae/41abCW4

This is another firm step in building a New Kerala committed to comprehensive and people-centred development.

On this day in 1959, the first nuclear reactor built solely for the purpose of medical research reached criticality. Operating at three megawatts thermal, the Brookhaven Medical Research Reactor (BMRR) at @BrookhavenLab was many times smaller than most power reactors. It was primarily used for research into a radiotherapy technique known as boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT). BNCT involves the selective targeting of cancer cells by irradiating boron compounds which have been placed within tumours. This treatment may be effective in treating brain cancers, such as glioblastoma multiforme. After years of supporting scientific research, the BMRR was shut down in December 2000.

Everything began with one man in the Cave of Hira. He wasn’t a king, nor rich. He was an orphan, unlettered, in an unlettered, ignorant society. He herded sheep, then traded. His name: Muhammad bin Abdullah ، peace and blessings be upon him. With no army, no bank, no internet, no passport ، in just 23 years he transformed 7 million square kilometers of dead desert into the largest connected empire in human history (from China to Spain). He defeated both the Persians and the Romans together in 15 years, while they possessed 90% of the world’s wealth at that time. He died while his armor was mortgaged to a Jewish man for 9 dirhams, and yet all the kings of the earth used to send him tribute and gold willingly. Is this power? No. This is the power of God that descended into the heart of one man. Every minute in the world, someone embraces Islam. 380,000 people send prayers on him in the same moment. 1.2 million people cry longing for him on TikTok and Instagram every day. The name “Muhammad” is the most given name in human history (over 150 million living males today). The influence of this great man has not stopped ، it grows faster than any virus, application, or empire. We have had 14 global empires that ruled more than 70 million km² at different times over 1400 years ، more than half of the inhabited world in their eras ، and all of them were subject to God then to one man they had never seen. He is the one before whom, after God, the necks of kings and emperors who ruled the entire world submitted, while they never saw him ،whether they were Arab or foreign emperors. Foreign kingdoms that did not share with him lineage, language, or culture still submitted to his message while never seeing him. What influence are you even talking about! And no matter how Islamic empires fall, they will rise again and continue, and this will remain until the Day of Resurrection. Look at this influence; look at this greatness. We will die, and every human breathing today will vanish, friend or enemy, but the one who remains is the name of this great man in the hearts of every human soul. Generation after generation will come to sacrifice themselves to raise the banner of monotheism ، the banner of God, the banner of our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. And after their lives end and they die, their grandchildren will rise again, and so on, until God inherits the earth and all who are upon it. Muhammad is not just a great man; Muhammad is the man who made greatness itself cry at his door for 14 centuries ، and it is still crying, and will cry until the Day of Judgment. This is only his influence ، we haven’t even touched on his life or his prophetic miracles. Wait ، and this is without even mentioning the Qur’an, which contains linguistic, historical, scientific, numerical miracles, and we haven’t touched on the laws, stories, and psychological aspects in it! Even non-Muslim orientalists submitted to his greatness and admitted his truthfulness and extraordinary influence, and placed him first globally. Yes ، after 1400 years, with the crowding of great figures, inventors, and geniuses over hundreds of years, he remained number one in “The 100: A Ranking of the Most Influential Persons in History” ،as testified by his enemies. All the heads of the world at one moment were humbled before a man who died 1000 years ago. He is the only man who broke the definition of “man” completely ،because he was the Messenger of God. Is he powerful? The answer: No ، he is the very power that shaped history with direct divine support. And for this reason, we call this being: the Master of the Universe.

Moscow's ideal scenario for a Middle East war is not a swift victory or a catastrophic escalation, but a conflict of moderate duration and intensity that keeps oil prices high without significantly disrupting the global economy. We are not there yet. Despite the oil windfall, the Kremlin is preparing budget cuts. The one untouchable area – military expenditure – remains predictably unaffected. The Bell (@thebell_io) ✂️ Oil Boom Won’t Shield Russia From Billion-Dollar Spending Cuts Despite the unexpected windfall of a Middle East conflict pushing oil prices higher, the Russian government has begun pressing ahead with sweeping spending cuts worth billions of dollars. “Spending cuts will kill the last bit of economic growth,” a senior official at the Ministry of Economic Development told The Bell. According to Vedomosti, at the start of the year Russia’s Finance Ministry notified all ministries of a 10% across-the-board reduction in spending. Bloomberg estimates the largest possible cut would amount to around 2 trillion rubles ($25 billion), or 0.8% of GDP — though The Bell’s own calculations suggest a more likely range of 0.5–1 trillion rubles ($6–12 billion). So-called “unprotected” budget lines will be first in line for cuts: national projects, infrastructure investment and road construction. Although the Finance Ministry wields considerable authority, sequestration is far from inevitable and is already facing pushback. “The plan is not to cut what is inflated, but what is left — and that’s just crumbs,” said one official at the Ministry of Economic Development. “This year, there is not much room. A transition period could be considered going forward,” a government official agreed. The cuts stem from structural long-term shortfalls. The budget rests on implausibly optimistic assumptions — oil at $59 a barrel, a rate of 92.2 rubles to the dollar — and authorities are banking on $15 billion from a VAT hike that looks increasingly unlikely to materialise amid slowing growth. ➡️ For the first three years of the war, the budget ran fat. Now, with belts tightening and the war still ongoing, civilian spending is the only lever left to pull — even as it has already been squeezed to the bone. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/thebell_io/status/2033597232268906825#m

Moscow's ideal scenario for a Middle East war is not a swift victory or a catastrophic escalation, but a conflict of moderate duration and intensity that keeps oil prices high without significantly disrupting the global economy. We are not there yet. Despite the oil windfall, the Kremlin is preparing budget cuts. The one untouchable area – military expenditure – remains predictably unaffected. The Bell (@thebell_io) ✂️ Oil Boom Won’t Shield Russia From Billion-Dollar Spending Cuts Despite the unexpected windfall of a Middle East conflict pushing oil prices higher, the Russian government has begun pressing ahead with sweeping spending cuts worth billions of dollars. “Spending cuts will kill the last bit of economic growth,” a senior official at the Ministry of Economic Development told The Bell. According to Vedomosti, at the start of the year Russia’s Finance Ministry notified all ministries of a 10% across-the-board reduction in spending. Bloomberg estimates the largest possible cut would amount to around 2 trillion rubles ($25 billion), or 0.8% of GDP — though The Bell’s own calculations suggest a more likely range of 0.5–1 trillion rubles ($6–12 billion). So-called “unprotected” budget lines will be first in line for cuts: national projects, infrastructure investment and road construction. Although the Finance Ministry wields considerable authority, sequestration is far from inevitable and is already facing pushback. “The plan is not to cut what is inflated, but what is left — and that’s just crumbs,” said one official at the Ministry of Economic Development. “This year, there is not much room. A transition period could be considered going forward,” a government official agreed. The cuts stem from structural long-term shortfalls. The budget rests on implausibly optimistic assumptions — oil at $59 a barrel, a rate of 92.2 rubles to the dollar — and authorities are banking on $15 billion from a VAT hike that looks increasingly unlikely to materialise amid slowing growth. ➡️ For the first three years of the war, the budget ran fat. Now, with belts tightening and the war still ongoing, civilian spending is the only lever left to pull — even as it has already been squeezed to the bone. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/thebell_io/status/2033597232268906825#m

Did you know 😏 He rubbed lemon juice on his face. Robbed two banks. Smiled at the cameras. Got caught in an hour. And changed psychology forever. In 1995, McArthur Wheeler walked into two banks in Pittsburgh and robbed them with no mask, no disguise, and lemon juice on his face. He believed that because lemon juice works as invisible ink on paper, it would make his face invisible to cameras. He smiled directly into the security cameras. Police aired the footage on the evening news and arrested him within an hour. When shown the tape, Wheeler stared at the screen and said, "But I wore the juice." He had tested the theory with a Polaroid selfie and didn't appear in the photo — because lemon juice got in his eyes and he aimed the camera at the ceiling. His case inspired Cornell psychologists David Dunning and Justin Kruger to publish their 1999 paper defining the Dunning-Kruger Effect — the cognitive bias where people with low ability drastically overestimate their own competence.

POR QUÉ LA FALTA DE DONANTES DE SANGRE ENCIENDE UNA SEÑAL DE ALERTA EN LOS HOSPITALES DE BUENOS AIRES En una entrevista, Alejandra Vellicce explicó en Infobae al Mediodía que en el Hospital de Clínicas se necesitan entre 30 y 40 donantes de sangre cada día para cubrir la demanda de pacientes, pero advirtió que resulta cada vez más difícil conseguir personas dispuestas a donar por el ritmo de vida actual y la falta de campañas de concientización. Durante su paso por el estudio de Infobae al Mediodía, donde dialogó con Maru Duffard, Andrei Serbin Pont, Jimena Grandinetti, Fede Mayol y Facundo Kablan, la especialista aseguró: “La sangre se necesita todos los días, y a veces estamos tan apurados que no nos ponemos a pensar en la importancia de donar”. La jefa de Hemoterapia explicó que los controles estrictos buscan proteger tanto al donante como al receptor: “Pedimos que pesen más de 50 kilos porque extraemos 450 mililitros, y controlamos con un pinchacito en el dedo si la cantidad de glóbulos rojos es suficiente”. Remarcó que muchos mitos impiden que potenciales voluntarios se acerquen a donar: “No hace falta concurrir en ayunas, esa es una de las causas más habituales de baja presión. Y si tenés tatuajes, solo debe haber pasado seis meses desde el último”. Sobre enfermedades crónicas, detalló: “Por ejemplo, los diabéticos insulino dependientes no pueden donar, pero si no usan insulina sí pueden”. 📲 Leé la nota completa 🔗 infob.ae/4sfrQta

What does Israel get from the Iran war? A prospect of their most powerful, arguably last remaining enemy being decimated by American hands. What the US gets out of it is another question. It was never about the nuclear program. But it wasn't about regime change either. Trump clearly doesn't care about that, as Venezuela's socialist government still in power demonstrates. The "imminent threat" framing is laughable goyslop, same as the tired mantras recycled from 47 years ago. Whatever the 47th president (wink wink) tried to achieve in the opening days of the war, he fell short, unless you consider killing a 90-year-old man and two hundred children a fair exchange for every US military base, greatest ally and vassal in the Middle East getting hit. So what has actually been achieved? Iranians have de facto closed the Strait of Hormuz, and the slow domino collapse of the "global economy" has begun. China, the EU, India, US-aligned East Asian states all depend on Middle Eastern oil. They've already been largely cut off from Russian energy, mostly by US hands. Whether anyone in Washington planned this or simply stumbled into it, either way the consequences are the same: rival economies are being strangled, and eventually they will have to beg the US to turn the tap back on. Or at least, that's what the Trump admin secretly hopes for. Trump meanwhile has "allowed" Russian oil and gas contracts until April and floated plans to "acquire Nord Stream", which they blew up. The logic of controlling the Strait eventually, and with it global energy supply, may well be present somewhere in the room. But it feels less like a master plan and more like someone connecting dots on a map they're drawing as they go, and that map is upside down. The caveats are significant. US troops navigating Iran's mountainous terrain could make Iraq look quaint by comparison, and the 2003-level readiness and troop numbers are simply not there. Trump is hemorrhaging popularity domestically, Democrats will likely take the midterms, and the Gulf state vassals are furious they took hits on America's behalf. The US depends on Taiwanese microchips that get more expensive in an energy crisis, which could halt the entire AI craze and drag the whole damn building with it. At this point, a full US withdrawal from the region isn't hard to imagine. If that were to happen, I truly feel for the Israelis biting their elbows while hiding in their mamads... Either way, I'm rooting for Trump to send as many troops into Iran as possible. Should be a fun and easy ride to Tehran.

Bolívia e Brasil estão unidos na preocupação com a segurança pública. O acordo que assinamos hoje renova nosso compromisso com o combate ao crime organizado nos dois lados da fronteira. Ele prevê maior coordenação para prevenir e punir o tráfico de drogas e de pessoas, contrabandos, roubos de veículos, lavagem de dinheiro, mineração ilegal e crimes ambientais. Ao mesmo tempo, é fundamental facilitar a mobilidade das pessoas. O presidente Paz e eu concordamos que a integração regional não é um projeto ideológico. É uma necessidade histórica. Em um mundo cada vez mais competitivo, nenhum país da nossa região terá condições de prosperar isoladamente. Somente uma América do Sul integrada poderá ocupar o lugar que merece na economia e na política global. Sem amarras ideológicas, sem ódio e sem violência, construiremos uma América Latina pacífica, integrada e próspera. @ricardostuckert

Outro pilar estruturante da parceria bilateral é a cooperação energética. Há décadas, a Petrobras ajuda a construir na Bolívia uma das mais importantes experiências de integração energética da América Latina. Em um contexto internacional marcado por conflitos que ameaçam a provisão segura de combustíveis, a Bolívia permanece como uma fonte segura e mantém a condição de maior fornecedor de gás natural para o Brasil. Conversamos sobre a possibilidade de ampliar investimentos nessa área e incrementar o volume exportado para o mercado brasileiro. O Gasoduto Brasil–Bolívia serviu muito ao crescimento da indústria brasileira e do setor de hidrocarbonetos boliviano. Hoje, ele pode ser aproveitado para uma integração mais ampla dos mercados de gás do Cone Sul. Também poderá contribuir para abastecer a fábrica de fertilizantes que o governo boliviano considera instalar em Puerto Quijaro. Também avançamos firmemente rumo à interconexão de nossos sistemas elétricos. O acordo que assinamos hoje abre caminho para a construção de linha de transmissão entre a província de Germán Busch, no departamento de Santa Cruz, e o município de Corumbá. 📸 @ricardostuckert

Somam-se a isso os investimentos robustos que continuamos fazendo para superar a carência de infraestrutura e fomentar a integração física com nossos vizinhos. Em 2004, inaugurei a primeira ponte entre Brasil e Bolívia, ligando Brasiléia, no Acre, a Cobija. Foi preciso aguardar mais de 500 anos para que nossos territórios fossem ligados por uma ponte. Ano passado, assinei a ordem de serviço para construir a segunda ponte entre nossos países, cujas obras terão início em 2027. A ponte sobre o rio Mamoré vai facilitar muito a vida dos moradores de Guajará-Mirim, em Rondônia, e Guayarámerin, no Departamento de Beni. Ela também é peça central para as Rotas de Integração Sul-Americana. Como parte do Quadrante Rondon, vai melhorar a conectividade dos produtores do Brasil e da Bolívia aos portos do Chile e do Peru, permitindo escoamento pelo Oceano Pacífico e acesso aos mercados asiáticos. Também queremos avançar em uma das aspirações que mobilizou vários governos bolivianos: obter acesso fluvial para o Atlântico. Com esse propósito, o Brasil apresentou ano passado projeto de acordo tripartite, com a Bolívia e o Paraguai, para aumento da navegabilidade da hidrovia do rio Paraguai, que inclui a dragagem, sinalização e balizamento do Canal Tamengo, que conecta a Lagoa de Cáceres a Corumbá.

Half Moon Bay’s second-biggest rocket enthusiast. Steve Jurvetson (@FutureJurvetson) 🚀 Today is the 100-year anniversary of the first liquid-fueled rocket launch. Like the Wright Brothers, Robert Goddard’s flight changed rocketry forever, pioneering today's mainstay, liquid-fueled SpaceX rockets. Here are my artifacts from his 1926 flight (last photo). But first, I am pointing to a museum replica of Nell — Goddard’s 10’ tall rocket powered by gasoline and liquid oxygen. It went just 41’ up in 2.5 seconds, hitting 60 MPH, but it marked the dawn of the space age. The New York Times publicly mocked his work in 1920, but Goddard persisted. Fearing further criticism, Goddard kept his 1926 launch secret for nearly a decade. Go Goddard, go, go go! “There can be no thought of finishing, for aiming at the stars, both literally and figuratively, is the work of generations, but no matter how much progress one makes there is always the thrill of just beginning.” — Robert Goddard From the Future Ventures’ space museum, last photo: 1) Inner nozzle from the first flight Starting on the far right, the alundum cement rocket nozzle liner from the liquid-fueled rocket launched by Robert H. Goddard, likely the world's first on March 16, 1926. The piece measures approximately 1.25 x 2.25 x .5 inches and has scorch marks on the interior from use. This artifact was given to Frederick C. Durant III by Goddard’s widow, Esther Goddard, and has been kept in an envelope labeled in Durant’s hand, “Ceramic rocket nozzle liner used by R. H. Goddard in 1920s, possibly from the 1926 (March 16) flight.” Frederick C. Durant III, the former head of astronautics at the Smithsonian’s National Air and Space Museum, was one of the world’s foremost authorities of spaceflight and rocketry. This is one of several artifacts he received from Esther Goddard, one of the four people on the crew for the launch of March 16, 1926, and from her testimony, he determined the 1926 flight as the likely origin. The small size of the piece lends credence to this conclusion, as Goddard’s rocket experiments grew larger and larger over time. 2) Fuel valve remains from a failed experiment Bottom left. Fuel-feed-rate needle valve from one of Goddard’s early rockets, circa late 1920s/early 1930s. The piece measures approximately 7 x 5 x 2” and consists of a valve passing through a longer pipe segment attached to a fragment of a larger base; a short bracket extends from the base, which was damaged in a blast during rocket experiments. The needle valves were located near the top of Goddard’s rockets and were a critical element in controlling his fuel feed line and tank systems. This artifact was given to Frederick C. Durant III by Goddard’s widow, Esther Goddard. 3) Fuel Tank Baffle Upper left. Bi-level metal rocket fuel tank baffle from one of Goddard’s early rockets, circa mid-to-late 1920s. The piece measures approximately 3.5″ in diameter and 2.25″ tall and consists of two discs connected by four rods. This artifact was also given to Frederick C. Durant III by Goddard’s widow, Esther Goddard. The baffle was an important element of Goddard’s fuel tank design, used to combat the ‘slosh’ of liquid propellant during flight. Three weeks into the war with Iran, a number of observations as someone who spent years war-gaming this scenario. 1. The U.S. and Israel may have produced regime transition in the worst possible way. Ali Khamenei was 86 and had survived multiple bouts of prostate cancer. His death in the coming years would likely have triggered a real internal reckoning in Iran, potentially opening the door to somewhat more pragmatic leadership, especially after the protests and crackdown last month. Instead, the regime made its most consequential decision under existential external threat giving the hardliners a clear upperhand. Now we appear to have a successor who is 30 years younger, deeply tied to the IRGC, and radicalized by the war itself – including the killing of family members. Disastrous. 2. About seven years ago at CNAS, I helped convene a group of security, energy, and economic experts to walk through scenarios for a U.S.--Iran war and the implications for global oil prices. What we’re seeing now was considered one of the least likely but worst outcomes. The modeling assumed the Strait of Hormuz could close for 4–10 weeks, with 1–3 years required to restore oil production once you factored in infrastructure damage. Prices could spike from around $65 to $175–$200 per barrel, before eventually settling in the $80–$100 range a year later in a new normal. 3. One surprising development: Iran is still moving oil through the Strait of Hormuz while disrupting everyone else. In most war games I participated in, we assumed Iran couldn’t close the Strait and still use it themselves. That would have made the move extremely self-defeating. But Iran appears capable of harassing global shipping while still pushing some of its own exports through. That changes the calculus. 4. The U.S. now finds itself in the naval and air equivalent of the dynamic we faced in Iraq and Afghanistan. It’s a recipe for a quagmire where we win every battle and lose the war. We have overwhelming military dominance and are exacting a tremendous cost. But Iran doesn’t need to win battles. They just need occasional successes. A small boat hitting a tanker. A drone slipping through defenses in the Gulf. A strike on a hotel or oil facility. Each incident creates insecurity and drives costs up while remind everyone that the regime is surviving and fighting. 5. The deeper problem is that U.S. objectives were set far too high. Once “regime change” becomes the implicit or explicit goal, the bar for American success becomes enormous. Iran’s bar is simple: survive and keep causing disruption. 6. The options for ending this war now are all bad. You can try to secure the entire Gulf and Middle East indefinitely – extremely expensive and maybe impossible. You can invade Iran and replace the regime, but nobody is seriously going to do that. Costs are astronomical. You can try to destabilize the regime by supporting separatist groups. It probably won’t work and if it does you’ll most likely spark a civil war producing years of bloody chaos the U.S. will get blamed for. None of these are good outcomes. 7. The other escalatory options being discussed are taking the nuclear material out of Esfahan or taking Kargh Island. Esfahan is not really workable. Huge risk. You’d have been on the ground for a LONG time to safely dig in and get the nuclear material out in the middle of the country giving Iran time to reinforce from all over and over run the American position. 8. Kharg Island can be appealing to Trump. He’d love to take Iran’s ability to export oil off the map and try to coerce them to end the war. It’s much easier because it’s not in the middle of IRan. But it’s still a potentially costly ground operation. And again. Again, the Iranian government only has to survive to win and they can probably do that even without Kargh. 9. The least bad option is the classic diplomatic off-ramp. The U.S. declares that Iran’s military capabilities have been significantly degraded, which is how the Pentagon always saw the purpose of the war. Iran declares victory for surviving and demonstrating it can still threaten regional actors. It would feel unsatisfying. But this is the inevitable outcome anyway. Better to stop now than after five or ten more years of escalating costs. Remember in Afghanistan we turned down a deal very early in the war with the Taliban that looked amazing 20 years later. Don’t need to repeat that kind of mistake. 10. The U.S. and Israel are not perfectly aligned here. Trump just needs a limited win and would see long-term instability as a negative whereas for Netanyahu a weak unstable Iran that bogs the U.S. down in the MIddle East is a fine outcome. If President Trump decided he wanted Israel to stop, he likely has the leverage to push it in that direction just as he pressured Netanyahu to take a deal last fall on Gaza. 11. When this is over, the Gulf states will have to rethink their entire security strategy. They are stuck in the absolute worst place. They didn’t start this war and didn’t want it and now they are taking with some of the worst consequences. Neither doubling down with the U.S. and Israel nor placating the Iranians seems overwhelmingly appealing. 12. One clear geopolitical winner so far: Russia. Oil prices are rising. Sanctions are coming off. Western attention and military resources are shifting away from Ukraine. From Moscow’s perspective, this war is a win win win. 13. At some point China may have a role to play here. It is the world’s largest oil importer, and much of that supply comes from the Middle East. Yes they are still getting oil from Iran. But they also buy from the rest of the Middle East, and a prolonged disruption in the Gulf hits Beijing hard. That gives China a real incentive to help push toward an end to the conflict.

Today marks the birthday of Albert Einstein, one of the most famous scientists in history. One cannot easily overemphasize the mark his famous equation (E = mc^2) left not just on nuclear physics, but in many other areas of scientific innovation. A @NobelPrize Laureate and @TIME's Person of the Century, Einstein exhibited throughout his life a nearly unparalleled depth of knowledge and insight into science. Among others, he explained the relationship between mass and energy, which became part of the most famous equation in the world: E=mc^2. Einstein’s work on atomic energy is embodied in the IAEA’s work today: he is often credited as being the first to recognize that atomic energy could indeed be unlocked, laying the foundation for modern nuclear science. His keen awareness of the atom’s power also led him to strongly advocate for atomic energy to only be used for peaceful purposes. The legacy of this remarkable scientist lives on as we pursue our mission at the IAEA to enlarge the contribution of atomic energy to peace, health and prosperity throughout the world.

However, in real-world driving conditions its recovery potential is limited by factors such as battery acceptance rate, speed range, and braking patterns. To address these limitations, I developed a patented (published) advanced energy recovery mechanism designed to go beyond conventional regenerative braking. This innovation focuses on improving how kinetic energy is captured and converted during vehicle operation, helping EV systems recover more usable energy and potentially increase real-world driving efficiency. Unlike traditional systems that depend mainly on motor-based regeneration, this approach introduces an additional recovery mechanism that can operate more consistently across different driving conditions. Key vision behind the innovation: • Enhance real-world EV energy efficiency, • Capture more usable energy during vehicle motion, • Reduce energy losses during braking and operation, • Support future EV platforms including cars, bikes, drones, and marine vehicles. As the EV industry moves toward higher efficiency and longer range, new energy recovery technologies will play a critical role in the next generation of electric mobility. This patented concept represents a step toward that future. 🔎Analyse de crédibilité : rumeurs sur la vie privée de Mojtaba Khamenei dans le contexte de la guerre informationnelle L’information trouve sa source primaire dans un article exclusif du New York Post publié le 16 mars 2026, relayé par une cascade de médias secondaires (WION, IranWire, IBTimes, OneIndia, etc.), et repose sur les déclarations de trois sources : deux officiels du renseignement américain et une troisième personne proche de la Maison Blanche, toutes affirmant que les agences d’espionnage américaines considèrent l’allégation comme crédible et non comme une opération de désinformation visant à fragiliser Mojtaba Khamenei. Le contenu central de l’allégation est le suivant : Mojtaba Khamenei aurait entretenu une relation sexuelle durable avec un homme qui fut son précepteur durant l’enfance , tandis qu’une troisième source diverge légèrement en indiquant que la personne concernée aurait plutôt été un employé de la famille Khamenei occupant une autre fonction, cette discordance entre sources affaiblissant la cohérence du récit. S’y ajoute l’allégation, non corroborée, selon laquelle Mojtaba Khamenei, blessé lors des frappes du 28 février qui ont tué son père, aurait, sous l’influence probable de puissants médicaments, effectué des avances sexuelles agressives envers ses soignants masculins. Sur le plan des éléments corroborants périphériques, un câble diplomatique américain de 2008, publié par WikiLeaks, mentionnait que Mojtaba avait épousé relativement tard, vers 30 ans, en raison d’un problème d’impuissance traité lors de plusieurs séjours prolongés dans des hôpitaux londoniens (Wellington et Cromwell), et qu’une quatrième visite de deux mois en Grande-Bretagne avait finalement été nécessaire avant que son épouse tombe enceinte, ce document évoque des problèmes médicaux mais ne mentionne en aucun cas l’orientation sexuelle, et sa réutilisation dans ce contexte relève d’une extrapolation. CBS News avait par ailleurs rapporté, sans préciser davantage, que le défunt ayatollah Ali Khamenei avait préféré un autre successeur en raison de certains « problèmes » non spécifiés dans la « vie personnelle » de son fils , ce qui constitue une convergence contextuelle notable mais non probante. La rumeur circulait déjà dans les cercles iraniens : son père et d’autres auraient soupçonné son homosexualité, et cette information aurait été propagée pour tenter de bloquer son accession au pouvoir , ce qui introduit un doute sérieux sur la motivation politique de la fuite. Sur le plan des limites majeures, les agences américaines ne disposent d’aucune preuve photographique ou vidéo, et aucun nom n’a été fourni ; la Maison Blanche n’a émis aucun commentaire officiel, aucune grande agence internationale indépendante (Reuters, AP, AFP) n’a confirmé l’information, et des responsables américains ont tenté de contenir la diffusion de cette information. Par ailleurs, le contexte géopolitique est lourdement chargé : les États-Unis sont en guerre ouverte avec l’Iran depuis les frappes de l’opération Epic Fury, Trump qualifie ouvertement Mojtaba de « lightweight » et d’« inacceptable », et la publication dans le New York Post, media à forte coloration éditoriale pro-Trump, via des sources anonymes au sein d’une administration engagée dans un conflit armé contre l’Iran constitue un facteur de décrédibilisation structurel majeur. En synthèse, la probabilité de véracité est à évaluer comme faible à modérée (30–40 %) : l’allégation peut être fondée sur un fragment de renseignement réel, mais elle est amplifiée, instrumentalisée et diffusée dans un cadre de guerre informationnelle manifeste, sans preuve matérielle vérifiable, avec des sources anonymes divergentes et une motivation politique évidente côté américain, ce qui en fait un élément à traiter avec une extrême prudence analytique.

It also ignores Israeli espionage inside the United States. A brief overview of both: First, the intelligence Israel provides Washington pertains to actors and conflicts only relevant to the United States because of the special relationship. The intelligence provided is on Israel’s adversaries. If Israel perceives them as threatening, it behooves Israel to provide the United States with this intelligence—they do not need American political, economic, or security incentives to do so. Moreover, this intelligence is often alarmist and politically motivated to push the United States toward confronting Israel’s enemies. Washington maintains a global intelligence apparatus more than capable of surveilling America’s adversaries without Israel. Second, there is a long history of Israeli espionage both inside the United States and targeting Americans abroad. The US intelligence community has highlighted this threat for decades—a leaked CIA document from 1979 discussing Israel’s foreign intelligence operations noted the United States is at the top of Israeli intelligence priorities, while US intel officials testifying to Congress in 2014 described Israel’s espionage activities in America as “unrivaled.” Israel and the lobby also go to great lengths to work around the Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) in their attempt to influence Washington. So long as Israel feels like it can continue such behavior without repurcussions, why would it ever stop? Industrial arable farming loses approximately 30 billion tonnes of topsoil per year globally. At current rates, we have about 60 harvests left before the soil that grows the world's crops is functionally depleted. Sixty harvests. About sixty years. Managed rotational cattle grazing builds topsoil at 1-2 inches per decade. Root systems deepen under grazing pressure. Manure feeds the soil biology. Hoof action increases water infiltration. Carbon moves from the atmosphere into the ground. This is how the North American Great Plains built six to eight feet of topsoil over millennia. Bison. Moving constantly. Never overgrazing any one area. The land thrived. Then we shot the bison, ploughed the grassland, planted continuous corn, and turned Kansas into a dust bowl within fifty years. The solution to topsoil loss is not fewer cattle. The solution to topsoil loss is more cattle, managed better, on more land. But that would require updating the narrative. The clock is ticking at thirty billion tonnes a year, and the narrative remains the priority.

Rt. Hon. Prime Minister Mrs. Sushila Karki attended the Closing Ceremony of the 12th NRN Global Conference and NRNA International General Assembly held in Kathmandu this evening. Addressing the Ceremony, the Rt. Hon. Prime Minister congratulated the newly elected Executive Committee of the NRNA and extended her best wishes for a successful tenure. The Prime Minister appreciated the important role played by the NRNA in connecting the Nepali diaspora across the world and underscored the significance of mobilising their knowledge, skills, capital and resources in contributing to Nepal’s economic wellbeing and overall development. Hon. Foreign Minister Mr. Bala Nanda Sharma, who chaired the Organising Committee of the 12th NRN Global Conference and NRNA International General Assembly, also congratulated the newly elected Executive Committee and thanked all concerned for their support and cooperation in making the conference a success. The three-day conference concluded today with the adoption of the 12-point Kathmandu Declaration. @pmsushilakarki @amritrai555 @lokbchhetri

Foreign Minister Mr. Bala Nanda Sharma held a telephone conversation with His Excellency Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the State of Kuwait, to discuss the evolving situation in the West Asia region. The Hon. Foreign Minister expressed concern over the attack on Kuwait’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and appreciated the efforts of the Government of Kuwait in maintaining stability and ensuring the safety and security of all residents, including the Nepali community. We praised its principles. We benefited from its predictability.” But, he added, “we knew the story… was partially false.” “The strongest would exempt themselves when convenient,” Carney said, arguing that “trade rules were enforced asymmetrically,” and “international law applied with varying rigor depending on the identity of the accused or its victim.” “We participated in the rituals. And we largely avoided calling out the gaps between rhetoric and reality.” That “pleasant fiction,” he states, no longer works. The new world is one where economic integration and financial infrastructure are openly used by hegemons—hinting at the United States—as “weapons” for “economic coercion.” Carney rejected reliance on bilateral deals with dominant powers. “When we only negotiate bilaterally with a hegemon, we negotiate from weakness,” he said. “This is not sovereignty. It is the performance of sovereignty while accepting subordination.” Instead, he called for “values-based realism,” urging middle powers to act together and build a third path that is not a “world of fortresses,” but partnerships with partners with shared standards. If you are not at the table,” Carney said, “you are on the menu.” His remarks were met with a rare standing ovation in the room. Full speech below. WHO condemns this tragic loss of life and emphasizes that health workers must always be protected. According to international humanitarian law, medical personnel and facilities should never be attacked or militarized. The intensification of conflict in Lebanon and the broader Middle East increases the likelihood of such tragedies. Urgent action is required to de-escalate the crisis and protect the health of people throughout the region.

पाणी फाऊंडेशनच्या सहकार्याने ‘पाणीदार महाराष्ट्र’ घडवण्याचा संकल्प मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यांच्या अध्यक्षतेखाली आज मंत्रालय, मुंबई येथे पाणी फाऊंडेशनच्या 'पॅन-महाराष्ट्र फार्मर कप'संदर्भात बैठक पार पडली. 'पाणी फाऊंडेशन'ने राज्य शासनासमवेत राज्याला बसणाऱ्या दुष्काळाची तीव्रता कमी करण्यात मदत केली असून यापुढेही पाणी फाऊंडेशनच्या सहकार्याने पाणीदार महाराष्ट्राचा संकल्प करुया, असे आवाहन मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यांनी यावेळी केले. मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस म्हणाले, हवामानविषयक संशोधन करणाऱ्या विविध संस्थांनी यावर्षी एल निनोचा प्रभाव जाणवणार असल्याचे मत व्यक्त केले आहे. त्यामुळे राज्यात 80 टक्के पाऊस होईल, असे गृहीत धरून जलसंधारणाच्या कामांचे नियोजन करावे. पाण्याचे महत्त्व ओळखून पाणी फाऊंडेशन काम करत आहे. या कामासाठी संबंधित शासकीय यंत्रणांनी फाऊंडेशनला मदत करावी. त्यासाठी पूरक यंत्रणा सज्ज ठेवावी. ही संस्था राज्यात करीत असलेल्या जलसंधारणाच्या कामांमध्ये मृद व जलसंधारण विभागाचाही समावेश करावा. यासह फाऊंडेशनच्या माध्यमातून होत असलेल्या कामाचा दर्जा चांगला राखण्यासाठी त्यांच्या मागणीनुसार नियंत्रण आणि पडताळणी यंत्रणेची आवश्यकता आहे. यासाठी कृषी सहाय्यक तसेच ग्रामविकास विभागाच्या उमेद अभियानातील कर्मचाऱ्यांचा समावेश असलेली व्यवस्था उभारण्यात यावी, असे निर्देश मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी दिले. यावेळी पाणी फाऊंडेशनचे संस्थापक आमिर खान आणि किरण राव, मुख्य कार्यकारी अधिकारी सत्यजित भटकळ आणि वरिष्ठ अधिकारी उपस्थित होते. @Dev_Fadnavis @paanifoundation #Maharashtra #DevendraFadnavis #PaaniFoundation

In a message released for the occasion of Eid al-Fitr, the leader of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan, Hibatullah Akhundzada, addressed political and international issues related to Afghanistan and the wider Muslim world. According to the statement, Akhundzada said the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan seeks to establish strong and positive relations with other Islamic countries based on Islamic brotherhood. He emphasized that the government wants diplomatic relations founded on Islamic principles and mutual respect. The Taliban leader also called on other countries to respect the values and traditions of the Afghan people and to refrain from interfering in Afghanistan’s internal affairs. In his message, Akhundzada further condemned what he described as unjust actions against Muslims around the world and violations of their rights.

A simulation that tells us a lot I want to share an exercise from 2002 that has a lot to do with the current war, but also shows how astute commanders didn't get the recognition they deserved. Today, Iran doesn't operate long or medium-range radars; it keeps almost all its equipment hidden inside mountains, including its planes, while deploying missiles, drones, and a asymmetric naval force. This is a war the U.S. doesn't know how to fight. Let me tell you a story, follow along: The Millennium Challenge 2002 (MC02) took place from July 24 to August 15, 2002, under the U.S. Joint Forces Command. Planned over two full years, it simulated a hypothetical 2007 scenario where the U.S. invaded a Middle Eastern country, clearly inspired by Iran or Iraq. The scale was massive: it cost $250 million and involved 13,500 personnel across 17 simulation sites and nine live locations. At the time, it was the largest and most expensive exercise in American history, designed to test the 'network-centric' warfare doctrine, featuring high-tech electronic surveillance and integrated command. Then came the twist: the opposing force, the 'Red Team' representing a simulated Iran, was led by retired Marine Corps Lieutenant General Paul K. Van Riper, a three-star general known for his unconventional tactics and for being 'devious' - shrewd and unpredictable. He was chosen specifically for that reason: to provide a realistic challenge. Van Riper did not disappoint. To bypass advanced U.S. electronic surveillance, he used 'old-school' asymmetric methods: motorcycle messengers for communication and World War II-style light signals, completely avoiding radars and digital systems. This neutralized the American command and control system, which relied heavily on cutting-edge technology. After receiving an ultimatum from the 'Blue Team' (the simulated U.S.) demanding surrender within 24 hours, Van Riper didn’t wait: he launched a devastating preemptive strike. In just 5 to 10 minutes, he used a massive salvo of cruise missiles combined with a fleet of small boats, including suicide attacks. The result? The Red Team sank 16 Blue Team ships: one aircraft carrier, ten cruisers, and five amphibious ships. In the real world, this would have equated to over 20,000 American military deaths, a total shock that paralyzed the exercise on the spot. But here is the part where you’ll understand the mistakes the U.S. is making today in fighting an asymmetric war with Iran: the exercise was abruptly halted, the sunken ships were 'refloated' as if nothing had happened, and the simulation was restarted with rigged rules. The Blue Team was given every advantage, and the Red Team was forced to follow a pre-written script with no freedom. Van Riper was forbidden from using his clever tactics: he was ordered to turn on anti-aircraft radars just so they could be destroyed, told not to shoot at 82nd Airborne aircraft or CV-22s, and even forced to reveal his unit positions. It was essentially a staged script to guarantee an American 'victory.' Outraged, the general resigned in protest, calling the whole thing 'propaganda' and 'scripted.'" Van Riper would be an ideal advisor for the situation in Hormuz, a situation for which I don't see even the slightest military solution.

This is not receiving enough attention: Qatar is the world's 2nd-largest helium producer, supplying ~33% of global output, at 63 million cubic meters in 2025. When Qatar's Ras Laffan facility, the world's largest LNG export plant, shut down due to the Iran war, helium supply was cut, as helium is extracted as a byproduct of natural gas processing. As a result, the market is now losing ~5.2 million cubic meters of helium per month, with almost no spare capacity globally, as helium evaporates during storage and must reach end users within ~45 days. The disruption has already DOUBLED helium prices since the Iran war began. If disruptions last 60 to 90 days, prices could surge another +25% to +50%, potentially exceeding $2,000 per thousand cubic feet, over 4 times early 2026 levels. The Iran war is disrupting far more than oil and gas.

IoT-Driven Water Management in Rural Tamil Nadu In Erode district, Tamil Nadu, an IoT-enabled smart water management system has been introduced to improve efficiency in rural water supply networks. Using sensors to monitor tank levels and automate pump operations, the system enables real-time management of overhead tanks and prevents overflow, ensuring more reliable water distribution. Deployed across 50 habitations in 16 villages, the solution has delivered a 40% reduction in electricity costs, 50% lower electricity consumption, and a 20% increase in water supply. In Ponmudi village alone, daily water availability increased by 44,180 litres. The initiative demonstrates how technology-led, institution-driven solutions can improve water efficiency, reduce operational costs, and strengthen sustainable rural infrastructure. #ChinaSeen The US One Voice Children's Choir performed the Chinese song "As Wished" at Beijing's Temple of Heaven. The touching performance quickly went viral online and captured the hearts of many Chinese viewers, drawing global attention to this historic landmark. The Temple of Heaven, located in the central axis of Beijing, served as a site for emperors to worship the heavens and pray for a bountiful harvest from the Ming (1368-1644) to Qing (1644-1911) dynasties. Listed as one of the UNESCO World Heritage, the Temple of Heaven covers 273 hectares, ranking as the largest extant sacrificial architectural complex in China. In terms of its overall layout and individual architecture, the Temple of Heaven reflects the relationship between heaven and earth, which stands the heart of ancient Chinese cosmology. The Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests is the main building of the Temple of Heaven, which was used to hold heaven worship ceremonies. The emperors prayed here for clement weather and an abundant harvest year.

Our railway network is the lifeline of the nation, but financial sustainability, delays in project execution, safety measures, and revenue generation remain key areas of concern. Under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme, 1337 railway stations were identified for phased redevelopment across the country, but only 172 stations have been completed so far. Keralam is not getting an adequate share in railway allocations. 1. The Budget 2026-27 mentioned the implementation of 7 high-speed railway corridors connecting cities in various states, but Keralam was not included. 2. There have been no sincere efforts from the Railways to complete the long-pending Angamaly–Sabari railway line. 3. The Railway connectivity to Nedumangad town could be provided through the extension of the Angamaly–Sabari railway line from Erumeli to Thiruvananthapuram. 4. The development project of the Neyyattinkara coaching terminal should be completed on priority. 5. Works on 7 Railway Over Bridges (ROBs) have not been started even after 12 years since sanction. 6. The demand for additional stoppages for passenger trains at Chirayinkeezhu and Kadakkavoor stations under the Attingal constituency should be considered. 7. A new train service from Thiruvananthapuram to Varanasi should be introduced for the convenience of pilgrims. : @AdoorPrakash ji in Lok Sabha Video

👉 This government has created two railways. One is the railway showcased in press meets and new launches - modern, premium, and highly publicized. The other is the railway used by ordinary people every day - delayed, overcrowded, and struggling with basic safety. 👉 Experts have noted that nearly ₹30 billion in recent years has gone toward station redevelopment and premium trains. But allocations for track renewal and safety remain minimal. What about maintaining the existing infrastructure that millions depend on every day? 👉 In my constituency, several electric trains cancelled during COVID-19 have still not been restored. People continue to suffer due to the lack of these essential services. 👉 Under the Amrit Bharat station renovation project in Tamil Nadu, 77 stations were taken up, but only 19 have been completed. People are asking how long these works will continue. 👉 The problem is clear: projects are sanctioned and funds are allocated, but execution is missing. I request the Railway Minister to release a clear timeline for completing these projects. : @s_kanth ji in Lok Sabha Video

In a message released for the occasion of Eid al-Fitr, the leader of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan, Hibatullah Akhundzada, addressed political and international issues related to Afghanistan and the wider Muslim world. According to the statement, Akhundzada said the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan seeks to establish strong and positive relations with other Islamic countries based on Islamic brotherhood. He emphasized that the government wants diplomatic relations founded on Islamic principles and mutual respect. The Taliban leader also called on other countries to respect the values and traditions of the Afghan people and to refrain from interfering in Afghanistan’s internal affairs. In his message, Akhundzada further condemned what he described as unjust actions against Muslims around the world and violations of their rights.

You do not need to crack NATO's systems if you can just text someone's old boss and ask nicely. The attackers focus on people who work in politics, the military, intelligence, or diplomacy, as well as journalists who cover security, defence, Russia, or Ukraine, lawyers or activists who deal with sensitive topics. It does not matter if the person currently holds a position or has retired, because someone who used to work in intelligence or NATO still has important contacts saved in their phone, and getting access to those contacts is the real goal. Signal is targeted on purpose, because these people use it precisely because they think it is safe, which makes them less careful than they would be on other platforms. Once an attacker takes over an account, they use it to to conduct secondary cyberattacks via acquired contacts - send phishing messages to everyone in the victim's contact list, pretending to be that person, which means the attack spreads outward and an entry point compromised target may become the door to much more important people in their network. The attack is elegant in a grim way. The more trusted you are, the more useful you become once compromised Lukasz Olejnik (@lukOlejnik) Ex-BND (German Foreign Intelligence Service) deputy chief Arndt Freytag von Loringhoven received a message from fake Signal “support” asking for his PIN. He typed it in. His contacts then got a malicious link through his hijacked account. He’s a former NATO intelligence chief, and the author of a book called Putin’s Attack on Germany, where he apparently covers Russian cyberattacks. The railway development in Keralam stands underrepresented, under-prioritized, and repeatedly overlooked. The share of railway infrastructure, travel facilities, and modernization projects allocated to the state remains grossly inadequate compared to other states. Keralam has consistently demanded a separate railway zone, the establishment of a coach factory, completion of automatic signaling, and full double-tracking of railway lines across the state. Unfortunately, despite years of appeals, discussions and assurances, these long-standing demands remain unfulfilled. The modernization works at Aluva railway station under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme remain incomplete even today, causing serious inconvenience to passengers. Similarly, development works at Angamaly and Chalakudy railway stations must be completed within a clearly defined timeframe. During the COVID-19 pandemic, several train stoppages at Aluva, Angamaly, and Chalakudy stations were withdrawn as a temporary measure. However, even after normalcy returned, they have yet to be restored. The government should provide additional train stoppages, complete the modernization work at Aluva railway station, and complete the construction work for the railway station near Cochin International Airport to ease passenger travel and improve connectivity. : @BehananBenny ji in Lok Sabha Video

【買取業務に関するご報告とお詫び】 本日、当店にて買取をご利用いただいたお客様より、「提出したカードが足りない」とのご指摘をいただきました。お客様は7枚提出されたとお申し出いただきましたが、当店側では当時5枚しか確認できず、査定担当者も「そのカードは見ていない」と回答いたしました。 その後、受付担当が防犯カメラの映像確認を提案し、査定担当者が該当の映像を確認。映っていた場面を写真で撮影し、お客様に提示いたしましたが、その映像には5枚しか映っていないように見えました。 その時点で受付担当は「映像で5枚しか確認できないため、納得いただけない場合は警察を呼んでご確認いただいた方が良いのでは」とお伝えしました。この発言はお客様への不信を前提としたものではありませんでしたが、結果として高圧的に受け取られかねないものであり、深く反省しております。 一度はお客様より「納得した」とのお言葉をいただきましたが、その数時間後「やはり足りないので再確認してほしい」とのご連絡をいただきました。PSAの鑑定番号も添えていただき、改めてより広い範囲の映像を確認したところ、お客様が査定物を出す準備の段階において、確かに7枚のカードをお出しになっていたことが確認されました。 結果として、査定担当者が7枚中5枚のみを査定し、残りの2枚を誤って査定済み用のケースに収納していたことが原因であったことが判明しました。このミスにより、お客様に不信感とご迷惑をおかけしてしまったことを、深くお詫び申し上げます。 今回の件では以下のような点が、お客様の信頼を損なう結果につながってしまいました： ①防犯映像が5枚に見えたという理由のみで、お客様のご申告を否定してしまったこと （映像には角度や映り方による限界があり、確定的な判断材料とすべきではありませんでした） ②「警察を呼びますか」といった対応が、誠実さではなく威圧と受け取られるような表現になってしまったこと ③映像確認の範囲が不十分で、カード提出の準備段階を確認していなかったこと （結果として「十分に確認もしていないのに、否定された」と感じさせてしまった可能性があります） お客様の大切なお品物をお預かりする立場として、あるまじき対応だったと真摯に受け止めております。 今後は以下のような再発防止策を徹底し、同様のことが起こらぬよう努めてまいります。 ・査定時のカード枚数を受付・査定・返却の各段階で必ず記録・照合 ・映像確認は受付〜準備段階〜査定開始までを通して行うことを明文化 このたびは、お客様に多大なご不快とご心配をおかけし、誠に申し訳ございませんでした。 今後とも誠実な対応と改善に努めてまいります。

Vuole commentare?” ✍🏻 I cittadini non devono cadere in questa trappola, nella quale più di qualcuno vorrebbe farli cadere. Devono andare a votare pensando a ciò che serve e che reputano più utile per l’Italia, non a ciò che conviene al Governo o ad un partito. E lo dico perché i governi passano, i partiti pure, ma la Costituzione rimane e incide sulla vita di tutti. Questa riforma non è di destra né di sinistra. È una riforma di semplice e puro buonsenso, e non è affatto un caso che molti dei punti che prevede – dalla separazione delle carriere al sorteggio per il Csm – siano stati proposti in passato da chi oggi li contesta con tanto impeto, col solo obiettivo di attaccare politicamente il Governo. Ma la verità è che questa riforma è una riforma giusta e che riguarda la vita di tutti, la nostra libertà e i nostri diritti. Dopo decenni di rinvii, tentativi falliti e occasioni mancate, siamo arrivati all’ultimo miglio. Il traguardo è in vista, ma riusciremo a tagliarlo solo se i cittadini ci daranno una mano. Iran war & the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has affected global oil supply & resulted in an LPG ‘crisis’ in India. #CutThe Clutter, with my colleague Udit Bubna, looks at India’s imports of LPG & LNG, how much we consume & measures undertaken by the Modi govt to address the concerns. 2. A large share of the world’s hydrocarbons — & a significant chunk of India’s gas imports — passes through the Strait of Hormuz. The tankers bring gas, which is liquified under pressure. So, they need to dock at specialised terminals. India only has a handful of such terminals & the major ones include Dahej, Hazira, Kochi, Dhamra, Ennore LNG Terminal. 3. India consumes about 189 million metric standard cubic meters of natural gas daily. Of this, 97.5 MMSCMD is produced domestically & 91.5 MMSCMD is imported. About 54% of what’s imported is currently under ‘force majeure’— a contract clause triggered by events beyond control (war, disasters). In India, Petronet LNG & GAIL have also issued various levels of ‘force majeure’ & that’s caused some panic. 4. India is the second largest consumer of LPG after China, using about 31 mn tons every year. We produce 40-45% domestically & about 55-60% is imported. Of the imports, 80-90% pass through the Strait of Hormuz. Usually, India sees about 55-60 lakh cylinder booking a day. This has now gone up to 75-80 lakh cylinders. If you use PNG at home, you’re relatively safe. 5. The prominent countries from where India imports crude oil are Russia, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Kuwait, UAE & all the Middle Eastern countries. Apart from that, we also import from the US, South Americas & Africas. That’s where the diversification has happened now — increasing countries from 27 to 40. 6. In February, India imported around 1.06 mn barrels/day from Russia, almost 1 mn barrels/day from Saudi Arabia & Iraq each. Now the Hormuz blockade affects the Middle East imports. So, what we’ve seen in just the first 10 days of March is a rise in imports from Russia — 1.59 mn barrels/day already. 7. शिक्षा से नौकरी तक... 2026 चुनाव में 'गेम चेंजर' बनेंगे 5.75 लाख Gen Z, पहली बार डालेंगे वोट चुनाव आयोग ने आज यानी 15 मार्च को विधानसभा चुनाव की तारीखों का ऐलान कर दिया है. इसमें चार राज्य- पश्चिम बंगाल, असम, तमिलनाडु, केरल और एक केंद्र शासित प्रदेश पुडुचेरी के विधानसभा चुनाव शामिल है. चुनाव की तारीखों की घोषणा के साथ ही राजनीतिक पारा हाई हो गया है. 2026 में होने वाले इस विधानसभा चुनावों में पहली बार वोट डालने जा रहे वोटर अहम भूमिका निभा सकते हैं. ऐसे में ये जानना जरूरी है कि इस बार कितने युवा मतदाता पहली बार अपना वोट डालने जा रहे हैं और इनके अहम मुद्दे क्या हैं? विधानसभा चुनावों में सबसे ज्यादा चर्चा युवा शक्ति की हो रही है. चुनाव आयोग के आंकड़ों के मुताबिक, इस बार 5.75 लाख युवा मतदाता पहली बार अपने वोटिंग अधिकार का इस्तेमाल करेंगे. 18 साल से ज्यादा उम्र वाले ये वोटर्स इस बार के चुनावी नतीजों को पलटने की ताकत भी रखते हैं. युवाओं के साथ-साथ इस बार 4.16 लाख दिव्यांग वोटर्स, 343 थर्ड जेंडर और 1.04 लाख सीनियर सिटीजन भी हिस्सा लेंगे. 2026 के विधानसभा चुनाव में युवा वोटर्स चुनाव के परिणाम को पलटने की ताकत रखते हैं. ऐसे में आइये जानते हैं क्या हैं युवाओं के अहम मुद्दे- नौकरी और बेरोजगारी- विधानसभा चुनाव 2026 में युवाओं के लिए सबसे बड़ा मुद्दा नौकरी और बेरोजगारी है. PIB के आंकड़ों और MoSPI की रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, भारत में बेरोजगारी दर 5% दर्ज की गई है. वहीं, 15-29 साल के युवाओं के लिए बेरोजगारी दर 14.7% रही है. ऐसे में इस बार युवा सरकारी नौकरियों और प्राइवेट सेक्टर्स में रोजगार की कमी का मुद्दे उठा सकते हैं. शिक्षा व्यवस्था- भारत दुनिया की दूसरी सबसे बड़ी शिक्षा प्रणाली है. लेकिन शिक्षा की गुणवत्ता के मामले में UNDP की रिपोर्ट के अनुसार भारत 134वें स्थान पर है. ऐसे में इस बार शिक्षा व्यवस्था पर युवा सवाल पूछ रहे हैं. युवा हायर एजुकेशन में सुधार, फीस कंट्रोल और स्कील डेवलपमेंट की मांग कर रहे हैं. कानून व्यवस्था- आज भी भारत में महिलाओं के प्रति अपराध एक चिंताजनक विषय बना हुआ है. महिलाओं के प्रति क्राइम में मामले लगातार बढ़ रहे हैं. NCRB 2023 रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, पिछले तीन सालों (2021-2023) के दौरान भारत में महिलाओं के खिलाफ लगभग 13.21 लाख मामले दर्ज किए गए हैं. ऐसे में इस बार युवा सुरक्षित वातावरण और महिलाओं की सुरक्षा को प्राथमिकता देने की मांग कर रहे हैं. महंगाई- दिन-ब-दिन बढ़ती कीमतों ने युवाओं पर भी असर डाला है. ऐसे में इस बार युवाओं का मुद्दा महंगाई भी है. महंगाई के कारण युवाओं के स्टैंडर्ड ऑफ लिविंग और फ्यूचर प्लानिंग पर असर पड़ रहा है. #GenZ #GenZVoters #Elections #Voting #TamilNadu #WestBengal #FirstTimeVoters

Prof. Ramesh Chand, Member, NITI Aayog, attended the Awards Ceremony organised by the Trust for Advancement of Agricultural Sciences at the National Academy of Agricultural Sciences Complex, New Delhi, as the Chief Guest. He presented the *Dr M. S. Swaminathan Award for Leadership in Agriculture (2025)* to globally renowned agricultural economist Prof. Prabhu Pingali, Professor of International Development Economics at Cornell University and Founding Director of the Tata-Cornell Institute for Agriculture and Nutrition. In his remarks, Prof. Chand described Prof. Pingali as among the top agricultural economists produced by India and recognised globally. He noted that while many economists focus on price policies and subsidies, Prof. Pingali’s work has uniquely focused on agricultural sciences, research and development, and innovation. He also highlighted the role of technology in making India a global food power in several areas, while noting the country’s continued import dependence in edible oils. #PMOIndia #NITIAayog #Agriculture #Innovation #AgriculturalResearch #FoodSecurity #NITIAayog

IoT-Driven Water Management in Rural Tamil Nadu In Erode district, Tamil Nadu, an IoT-enabled smart water management system has been introduced to improve efficiency in rural water supply networks. Using sensors to monitor tank levels and automate pump operations, the system enables real-time management of overhead tanks and prevents overflow, ensuring more reliable water distribution. Deployed across 50 habitations in 16 villages, the solution has delivered a 40% reduction in electricity costs, 50% lower electricity consumption, and a 20% increase in water supply. In Ponmudi village alone, daily water availability increased by 44,180 litres. The initiative demonstrates how technology-led, institution-driven solutions can improve water efficiency, reduce operational costs, and strengthen sustainable rural infrastructure. The 2026 edition of @TakshashilaInst's flagship Conference, 'Takshashila Network for Advanced Studies', concluded with some of the most pragmatic and insightful discussions on China, Pakistan, Technology Geopolitics & Law Enforcement. Not only were the parallel Fellowship tracks filled with engaging and interactive sessions with some of the best minds in respective fields, but also the plenaries and group events were wholesome & stimulating. For me, managing the China track alongside @BhumikaSevkani and @am_i_t_kumar, and with @theChinaDude's guidance, was a delight. Some key takeaways from the discussions are: #1 China's security ambitions and arms sales are deeply interlinked with those of the United States. China pits its capabilities against the US, though its intention to go global doesn't necessarily mean it has the capability to fill any vacuum the US may be leaving behind. #2 There is no doubt that China innovates. But sanctions are likely to slow China's roll. For countries that lead in innovation, the goal of imposing tech denials is not so much to ban technology flows as to delay them, using the lead time to diffuse the technology into productive sectors across their economy & translating the tech lead into more pervasive national power. #3 The long arc of China's post-1959 engagement with and eventual control of Tibet begins with establishing a digital and informatised surveillance infrastructure, extends to policymakers seeking control over religion and ideological legitimacy, and eventually induces the CPC's purported dominance in Buddhism as an element of G-2-G engagements. #4 India's most important policy question today should be countering Chinese involution and trade dumping practices without relying overtly on industrial subsidies, which are now under the global radar due to China's actions in the past many decades. Further, for all regions of the world, China's own strategy for the next five years is not to allow traditional manufacturing and jobs to take flight elsewhere. Strategies must be developed to create a collective network or layered trade agreements in advanced manufacturing. Watch out this space for more, until next time!
